uncited: This family defines methods for determining the intersection between a ray and a surface defined implicitly by a scalar field $f(\mathbf{x})$ (where the surface is the zero-level set $f(\mathbf{x})=0$) or a Signed Distance Field (SDF).
It solves the problem of finding the nearest point $\mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}$ such that $f(\mathbf{o} + t\mathbf{d}) = 0$ without relying on explicit triangle meshes.

It is distinguished from [General Ray-Triangle Intersection](909-general-ray-triangle-intersection-pl-cker-coordinates.md) by its reliance on function evaluation rather than geometric primitives, and from [Sphere Intersection](1620-sphere-intersection.md) by its generality, requiring numerical root-finding or traversal rather than closed-form quadratic solutions for arbitrary functions.
The problem of intersecting rays with implicit surfaces is fundamental to ray tracing and volume rendering, allowing for the rendering of complex shapes without explicit mesh representation.
Early work focused on robust root-finding for algebraic surfaces.
In the context of fluid simulation and collision detection, SDFs are widely used.
